findings.claim: While the name filter is active, the new effect at FolderBrowser.tsx:618-620 runs `keepOnly(visibleFileIds)` on every change of `files`, including list reloads that briefly empty `files`. Each such reload clears the whole selection and the Shift anchor, even though the filter has hidden nothing.
findings.impact: Example: with the name filter in use, a batch Move to Trash or Purge ends partial or stopped. SelectionBar then holds the failed and unconfirmed ids through `onSelectOnly(kept)` and shows the 'N done / M failed' outcome with a retry. It immediately calls `onComplete(true)` → `refresh()` → `reset()` → `files = []` → `keepOnly([])`, so the selection drops to 0. SelectionBar returns null at count 0, and the failure report and the retry disappear. The user is not told that some files were not deleted. The same wipe hits any hand-built selection under the filter whenever a websocket `drive.structure_changed` or `drive.file_updated` event, or any other `refresh()`, reloads the list. With the filter empty, the selection survives these reloads as it did before.
findings.evidence: FolderBrowser.tsx:187-191 derives `visibleFileIds` from `nameFilter.files`, which is a memo over `files` (useFolderFilter.ts:47-53). FolderBrowser.tsx:618-620: `useEffect(() => { if (nameFilter.isActive) keepOnly(visibleFileIds) }, [nameFilter.isActive, visibleFileIds, keepOnly])`. `isActive` depends only on debouncedText (useFolderFilter.ts:64), so it stays true across a reload. FolderBrowser.tsx:125: `refresh` bumps refreshKey. useFolderFiles.ts:809-819: a refreshKey or websocket bump calls `reset()`. useInfiniteScroll.ts:120-131: `reset` calls `setItems([])`. useFolderFiles.ts:750/756: for a plain folder, `files` is `paginatedFiles`, so it becomes `[]`. useSelection.ts:59-68: `keepOnly([])` empties the set and nulls the anchor. SelectionBar.tsx:203-213: on partial or stopped, it calls `onSelectOnly(kept)`, then `onComplete(true)`. FolderBrowser.tsx:969-976: with `clearedSelectionRef` empty on this path, `onlyContinuation` is false, so `refresh()` runs. SelectionBar.tsx:143: `if (count === 0) return null`. After the reload, only page 1 (limit 30) comes back, so the cleared ids are not restored either.
findings.repro: Not run (read-only tools). Steps: open a folder, type a name filter, enter selection mode, select several shown files, and Move to Trash while one of them fails (or press Stop mid-run). Expected: the failed ids stay selected with the partial outcome and retry. Predicted: the bar vanishes after the refresh. Test-level mutation: in FolderBrowser.selectionFilter.test.tsx, make the mocked useFolderFiles return `files: []` for one render after the filter is set, then FILES again. A selection made under the filter is lost, and all four existing tests still pass because they never change `files`.

bucket_proposal.reason: Pruning is keyed on the derived visible-id list, which changes both when the filter hides a row and when the list reloads. A fix needs another condition to tell those apart, such as pruning only on a debouncedText change, or skipping while loading or while `files` is empty. That is the design patching itself again rather than a local slip. No invariants file exists, so A is unavailable.

findings.proposed_fix: Prune only when the filter text (debouncedText) changes, or when a row the filter shows leaves the shown set while the same rows are still loaded. Do not prune on reloads of `files`. Alternatively, derive the effective selection at use sites (selected ∩ visible) instead of mutating stored selection state. Add a test where `files` empties and refills under an active filter.

specification_compliance: No invariants file exists for this change. docs/process/reviews/fix-select-all-respects-name-filter/ holds decisions.md (an R-5 in-app walk at d5123d37d) and the review directories. So there is no declared list to check the diff against, and bucket A is unavailable.

The R-5 walk in decisions.md exercises Select all, Shift range and filter-hides-selected on a five-file folder. Its batch trash in step 2 completed fully, so it never took the partial or stopped `onSelectOnly` + `refresh()` path where the finding bites.
The commit under review, ac9090203, is docs-only. The only code change since r2 is d5123d37d: `useSelection.keepOnly` plus the pruning effect in FolderBrowser.
potential_unspecified_behavior: Whether the selection should survive a list reload (websocket structure or file_updated event, refresh after a bulk action) while the name filter is active is not specified. The base keeps it; the change now clears it.
FolderBrowser.tsx:792 still passes the toolbar `fileIds={files.map(...)}` from the unfiltered list to addon bulk-action slots. This is pre-existing and not touched.
handlePlayAll and hasPlayableFiles still read the unfiltered `files`, so Play all can start on a row the filter hides. This is pre-existing.
Renaming a selected file (inline) so that it no longer matches the filter now drops it from the selection silently. This is consistent with the stated UNSPEC, but no test covers it.
regression_risks: Any `files` identity change re-runs the pruning effect while the filter is active. Additions such as pagination and favorite toggles are no-ops (keepOnly returns `prev` when the size is unchanged). Removals and resets prune, and a reset to [] prunes everything. See the finding.
keepOnly nulls `lastToggledIdRef` synchronously in the effect, so after any reload under the filter the next Shift-click selects only the clicked row instead of a range.
Filter state lives in FolderBrowser since the first commit, so it outlives the FolderContent unmount on the passages toggle (noted in r2; unchanged).
test_coverage: FolderBrowser.selectionFilter.test.tsx mocks useFolderFiles with a constant FILES array, so `files` never changes under an active filter. A mutation that clears the selection whenever `files` changes (which is what the current code effectively does on reset) survives all four tests.

The 'drops a selected file when the filter comes to hide it' and 'Shift after the anchor was hidden' tests would fail if the effect or the anchor-null branch in keepOnly were removed, so the intended pruning is covered.
No useSelection unit test for keepOnly was added: the `next.size === prev.size ? prev : next` identity return and the anchor reset are covered only through the FolderBrowser integration tests.
No test covers the SelectionBar partial or stopped outcome together with an active name filter.
not_verified: I did not run the test suite, the type checker, or the app. The finding is traced from code, not reproduced.
I did not confirm whether React batching could leave `files` non-empty during reset in some path (for example, hydration with revalidateInitial), which would narrow the trigger.
I did not check which backend actions emit `drive.file_updated` in ordinary use (the media_import addon and event_hooks.py emit it), so how often the websocket path fires is not established.
I did not read CLAUDE.md or docs/process/*.md in full. Conventions were inferred from decisions.md and the review record only.
trajectory: r1 → r2: no code change; a3c4b533b is docs-only. r2 → r3: d5123d37d is the only code fix. On top of the first commit's derived `visibleFileIds` (a stateless derivation), it adds a stored-state reconciliation: a useEffect that mutates the selection to match the derived list, plus a new branch in `keepOnly` that resets the Shift anchor. ac9090203 is docs-only. So the code fix adds a state-sync mechanism and a branch that the earlier round did not have; it removes none. The finding above shows that this effect cannot tell 'the filter hid a row' from 'the list reloaded'. The natural fix adds yet another condition (debouncedText-change or loading guard), so the design is being patched rather than settled.
